assessments.technical_explanation: The flagged lines are scoped CSS selectors for Vue toast-notification transition animations. They control opacity and a small vertical shift when a notification enters or leaves the screen. There is no registry, startup, autostart, or persistence mechanism anywhere in the file; the scanner keyword match on the animation class names is a false positive.
assessments.layman_explanation: The flagged lines are styling rules that make popup messages fade and slide in and out on the profile page. They have nothing to do with making anything run at startup or persisting anything.

assessments.technical_explanation: The match is a documentation file, not shipped code. The flagged example fetches a model list from the user's own local image-generation daemon on a loopback address and pipes the response through a standard JSON formatting module that only parses and pretty-prints text; it does not interpret or execute the downloaded content. The guide is proportional to the project's stated purpose of connecting to a local image backend, and nothing downloads and runs code.
assessments.layman_explanation: This is a setup guide that shows how to check what image models your own locally running image tool offers. The command shown only formats the reply for easier reading; it never runs the downloaded data as a program. Nothing harmful is demonstrated.

assessments.technical_explanation: The session token from the client auth store is attached as a bearer authorization header on requests to a same-origin relative API path belonging to the application's own backend. This is the standard authentication pattern for a self-hosted client-server app: the credential is used only to authenticate the user to the same server that issued it, with no hardcoded external destination, third-party host, telemetry sink, or obfuscated routing anywhere in the supplied file. Co-location of a credential source and a network call is expected in any authenticated client composable and does not demonstrate exfiltration.
assessments.layman_explanation: This part of the app attaches your login token to requests it sends to the app's own server so the server knows who you are. That is the normal way a logged-in app talks to its own backend. The token is never sent anywhere else, so there is no sign of credential theft.

assessments.technical_explanation: This line completes the same scoped CSS transition rule, setting the hidden start and end states for the toast animation. No executable behavior, destination, or persistence mechanism is involved.
assessments.layman_explanation: The last piece of the popup message animation styling; purely visual with no persistence effect.

assessments.technical_explanation: The flagged references to the runtime environment variable are confined to a linting configuration file used only during development. They toggle two lint rules on or off depending on whether a production build is being checked. There is no serialization of sensitive values, no transmission, and no runtime execution in the shipped application; the signal is a keyword-level false positive on standard tooling configuration.
assessments.layman_explanation: This is a code-quality checker configuration that looks at one harmless environment marker to decide how strict it should be. It reads no secrets, sends nothing anywhere, and never runs in the finished app.

The obfuscation signal appears to be a false positive from the parser's dense regular-expression literals; nothing in the data flow conceals behavior.
